Thank you for choosing Calculator++!\n\nCalculator++ is a powerful tool for making everyday calculations.
Gives absolute value of an argument
Converts degrees from DMS notation to decimal notation: d - degrees, m - minutes (default = 0), s - seconds (default = 0)
Equals function - gives 1 if two arguments are equals, otherwise 0
Greater-or-equals function - gives 1 if two arguments are equals or the first is greater than the second, otherwise 0
Greater function - gives 1 if the first argument is greater than the second, oherwise 0
Lesser-or-equals function - gives 1 if two arguments are equals or the first is less than the second, otherwise 0
Natural logarithm - logarithm to base e
Lesser function - gives 1 if the first argument is less than the second, otherwise 0
Not-equals function - gives 1 if two arguments are not equals, otherwise 0
Converts degrees into radians: d - degrees, m - minutes (default = 0), s - seconds (default = 0)
Gives the sign of an argument: -1 if an argument is less than 0, 0 if equals to 0, 1 if more than 0
Gives derivative of order \'order\' (default = 1) of functions \'f(x)\' by \'x\' variable and calculates at point \'x_point\' (default = same as \'x\')
Gives integral of function \'f(x)\' by \'x\' variable
Integrates function \'f(x)\' by \'x\' variable from \'a\' to \'b\'
Modulo operation finds the remainder of division of \'x\' by \'y\'
Gives product of functions \'f(i)\', iterating through \'i\' from \'from\' to \'to\'
Sums functions \'f(i)\', iterating through \'i\' from \'from\' to \'to\'
Gives the double factorial of the previous expression
Gives the factorial of the previous expression

Gives the percent value of the expression before.
Examples:
 100 + 50% = 150
 100 * 50% = 50
 100 + 100 * 50% * 50% = 125
Value must be either a number or left empty: if you have parameters - create a function instead!

The gravitational constant is an empirical physical constant involved in the calculation of the gravitational attraction between objects with mass, m^3·kg^−1·s^−2
Ratio of any circle\'s circumference to its diameter. Note: this constant is degree unit dependent => rad: 3.14, deg: 180.0
Speed of the light in vacuum, m/s
Unique real number such that the value of the derivative (slope of the tangent line) of the function f(x) = e^x at the point x = 0 is equal to 1
Imaginary unit, defined such as i^2 = −1
Ratio of any circle\'s circumference to its diameter. Note: this constant is degree unit independent => rad: 3.14, deg: 3.14
